account:
It is day 1, ten o'clock, and I have reached the mill for the scheduled grain inspection. No one has yet shown me the grain stocks. The secretary reported no new correspondence, council letters, resident repair requests, or business requiring a decision. Freight's proposal remains on file, with no delivery authorized. Builder reported that the bridge was passable and lanterns were present, and had no specific defect or itemized repair estimate. I have authorized no paid repairs or purchases.

The unusual news is a repeated report of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 01 now says baker and freight were there, and also reports baker, freight, and neighbour together there. Other nearby townsfolk have repeated the same phrase, but I cannot tell whether these are independent observations or circulating gossip. I have not witnessed the discussion or learned what change was proposed, when it happened, or whether anything was agreed.

Residents also reported baker carrying sacks of bread at the inn and bakery, and wheat at the bakery. Those movements could be ordinary baking and delivery work; they are not evidence of misconduct. Combined with freight's involvement and the mention of bridge or port changes, the bakery discussion may concern transport or bread and grain distribution. That is only a working hypothesis. It could be private business rather than town policy. I should ask baker, freight, and neighbour what was actually discussed, and whether any public crossing or delivery arrangements are intended to change, without treating the rumour as an established decision. I have asked the secretary to distinguish firsthand reports from rumours and tell me privately about unusual town business.
